resolutions.summary: Claim narrowed to what is true, and pinned on the real xom-2021 in-cell images. ADR-033 gains a new subsection b2a stating the actual rule: an image offset is a reading-order point, a table/cell span is tightened to VISIBLE TEXT (ADR-029 b1) and an image contributes none, and an empty cell is then clamped into the tightened table span -- so an image in a text-carrying cell does land inside that cell, while an image in an image-only cell that precedes the table's visible text lands outside the whole table. b1's unconditional sentence now points at b2a instead of asserting the false half, and g's synthetic-shape list says which of the two _demo pins.
resolutions.why_not_the_other_option: Changing the placement so an in-cell image lands inside its cell was the acceptance's alternative and is rejected on the merits: pulling a table span back to swallow an image would break ADR-029's rule that a table span is tight to its own text (and its `tables_sane` tightness assertion), and moving the image offset would make it something other than where the image is. Both would also move committed table offsets for a frozen capability. The relationship is real and simply had to be asserted rather than assumed.

resolutions.new_vocabulary: the `image` check gains one optional key, `in_table` (src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py), asserting whether the offset lies inside some recorded table span; it refuses rather than guesses when the case did not also ask for tables. Unit-covered both ways plus the refusal in test_eval_adapter.py::test_image_checks.
